stories.headline: Fresh monsoon rains trigger floods, landslides and highway closures across Nepal, six dead
stories.summary: Continuous rain since Asoj 8 (around Sept 24) has caused floods and landslides across Bagmati, Lumbini, Gandaki and Karnali provinces, with central police spokesperson Abinarayan Kafle confirming six deaths and 407 rescues. Major highways including the East-West Highway, BP Highway, Karnali Highway, Kanti Lokpath and Jomsom-Korala road have been blocked by landslides, while rivers including Koshi, Narayani, Tinau and Seti have crossed alert or danger levels, prompting evacuations and permit suspensions in Mustang.

stories.headline: Humla records heaviest rainfall in nearly five decades
stories.summary: The Meteorological and Hydrological Office in Surkhet, per office chief Dr Indira Kandel, recorded 114.8mm of rain in Simikot, Humla over 24 hours from Sept 25 to 26, the highest since 1978 (46-48 years). The record-breaking rain is linked to a westerly moisture system affecting Karnali province.

stories.headline: PM Balendra Shah returns from UN General Assembly, calls for climate justice and LDC graduation extension
stories.summary: Prime Minister Balendra Shah addressed the 81st UN General Assembly's high-level week, urging climate justice and compensation after Nepal's deadly floods and proposing an extension to Nepal's LDC graduation timeline and a 'Himalayan Mechanism', according to Nepal government and multiple outlets. He returned to Kathmandu on Saturday.

stories.headline: One month after Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods, recovery remains slow and displaced people still struggling
stories.summary: A month after the deadly Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods, some roads and bridges have been temporarily reconnected but reconstruction is far from complete, per Nepal Press; OnlineKhabar reports holding centres emptying as survivors move in with relatives after receiving only basic relief. International outlets including Telegraph India and BBC report large disputed casualty and missing-person figures from the disaster, underscoring how much remains unverified a month on.

stories.headline: Nepali Congress Deuba faction accelerates preparations for 15th general convention
stories.summary: The Sher Bahadur Deuba-aligned faction of Nepali Congress says it has finalised roughly 775,000 active memberships and published an online portal, with ward conventions planned from Asoj 15 and a central convention set for Mangsir 21-23, according to Nagarik News and OnlineKhabar. A rival establishment-linked faction, per Ratopati, says it will hold its own 15th general convention in November, with leaders like Shashank Koirala calling it a major test for the party.

stories.headline: Nepal has mixed results at Asian Games: cricket advances, badminton and other events end campaigns
stories.summary: At the ongoing Asian Games in Japan, Nepal's men's T20 cricket team has reached the quarterfinals, per Setopati, while badminton player Kshitiz Khanal was eliminated in the round of 32 after losing to Iran's Nima Rostampour, according to Nepal Press and Ratopati. Separately, Nepali bodybuilder Sagendra Singh won gold at the Asian Bodybuilding Championship, per The Rising Nepal.

advocate.argument: This is a fast-moving, multi-province disaster story with an official casualty count (six dead, two injured, 407 rescued) attributed by name to central police spokesperson Abinarayan Kafle, corroborated across Nepal Press, DC Nepal, Ratopati, Nagarik News and Republica. It combines hard numbers with tangible, checkable disruption: East-West Highway blocked near Kapilvastu, BP Highway damaged at eight Kavre locations, Karnali Highway and Kanti Lokpath cleared but still risky, Jomsom-Korala and Solukhumbu links cut, and rivers (Koshi, Narayani, Tinau, Seti) above alert/danger levels with barrage gates opened. Mustang's permit suspension and Pokhara's Ramghat lake-formation add local colour. The story sits inside a larger, already-tracked 2026 monsoon disaster arc (Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods, NEPSE investor jitters), so readers have context and stakes. It affects transport, tourism, agriculture and safety nationwide — a genuine public-service story with wide geographic reach for both domestic and diaspora audiences worried about home regions.
